trivia.q: Which pharmaceutical company put heroin on the market in 1898 as a cough remedy and 'non-addictive' morphine substitute?
trivia.note: Same people who brought you aspirin. One of those worked out.

trivia.q: Coca-Cola stopped using fresh coca leaves, and with them most of the cocaine, in roughly what year?
trivia.note: They used 'spent' leaves after that. Spent, like your uncle on Christmas Eve.

trivia.q: Pervitin, handed out to German soldiers by the millions in World War II, was which drug?
trivia.note: Blitzkrieg had a secret ingredient, and it was tweaking.

trivia.q: Until 1948, 7 Up contained which mood stabilizer in its formula?
trivia.note: The 'Up' was doing a lot of work.

trivia.q: Fentanyl was first synthesized around 1960 by which Belgian chemist?
trivia.note: His company still makes it. Legally, mostly.

trivia.q: The FDA approved naloxone for opioid overdose in what year?
trivia.note: It took another five decades to put it on a gas station shelf.

trivia.q: 'Krokodil,' the Russian street drug that rots skin into scales around the injection site, is which opioid?
trivia.note: Homemade from codeine, gasoline, and whatever was under the sink.

trivia.q: Albert Hofmann first synthesized LSD in what year, five years before he accidentally dosed himself?
trivia.note: He biked home afterward. There's a holiday for it.

trivia.q: AA co-founder Bill Wilson personally experimented in the 1950s with which drug as a possible aid to recovery?
trivia.note: This does not come up at the Tuesday meeting.

trivia.q: Alcoholics Anonymous was founded in 1935 in which city?
trivia.note: Two drunks and a kitchen table in Ohio. Twelve steps later, here we are.

trivia.q: Methadone was first developed in the late 1930s in which country?
trivia.note: Not named after Hitler. That rumor is a lie your sponsor told you.

trivia.q: Kratom comes from a tree in the same botanical family as which everyday plant?
trivia.note: Both sold at the gas station, both ruin your sleep, only one ruins your liver.

trivia.q: Which of these is a Schedule II drug still prescribed in the US under the brand name Desoxyn?
trivia.note: Approved for ADHD and obesity. Your doctor will not write it.

trivia.q: Which drug is legally used by US surgeons as a topical anesthetic in nose and throat procedures?
trivia.note: Schedule II. The ENT has a locked box and a straight face.

trivia.q: In the UK, heroin is legally prescribed for severe pain under what name?
trivia.note: The NHS will give you heroin. You just have to be dying correctly.

trivia.q: Withdrawal from which of these drugs can, by itself, kill you?
trivia.note: Heroin withdrawal makes you want to die. Alcohol withdrawal does it for you.

trivia.q: 'Wet brain,' or Wernicke-Korsakoff syndrome, is caused by a deficiency of which vitamin?
trivia.note: Hence the banana bag. Hence the yellow IV. Hence the guy who thinks it's 1994.

trivia.q: Carfentanil, found in street heroin, was developed as a tranquilizer for which animals?
trivia.note: About 10,000 times the potency of morphine. You are not an elephant.

trivia.q: Xylazine, 'tranq,' is a sedative approved only for which use?
trivia.note: Narcan doesn't touch it. Neither should you.

trivia.q: Who won the 1949 Nobel Prize in Medicine for inventing the lobotomy?
trivia.note: The Nobel committee has never taken it back.

trivia.q: Walter Freeman's quick 'transorbital' lobotomy went in through the eye socket using what tool?
trivia.note: From his own kitchen, originally. Ten minutes a patient.

trivia.q: The original 'Body Farm,' where donated corpses decompose for forensic research, is run by which university?
trivia.note: Behind the hospital in Knoxville. Great place to get your steps in.

trivia.q: In what year did the American Psychiatric Association remove homosexuality from the DSM?
trivia.note: Caffeine withdrawal is still in there.

trivia.q: Which of these is an official DSM-5 diagnosis?
trivia.note: Yes. Your Monday headache is billable.

trivia.q: What over-the-counter drug is the leading cause of acute liver failure in the US?
trivia.note: Tylenol. The one your detox roommate took twelve of for a hangover.

trivia.q: Viagra was originally developed to treat what?
trivia.note: Trial subjects reported a side effect. Pfizer pivoted.

trivia.q: Rogaine's active ingredient, minoxidil, was originally approved as a pill for what?
trivia.note: Patients got hairy. Marketing got ideas.

trivia.q: In the 1920s and 30s, Lysol was heavily marketed to American women as what?
trivia.note: Ads winked that it prevented pregnancy. It prevented tissue.

trivia.q: Listerine's 1920s ads invented a medical-sounding condition to sell mouthwash. What was it?
trivia.note: The word for bad breath was a marketing campaign. So was your self-esteem.

trivia.q: Mrs. Winslow's Soothing Syrup, sold for teething babies in the 1800s, contained what?
trivia.note: The AMA filed it under 'Baby Killers.' It kept selling.

trivia.q: JFK's 'Dr. Feelgood,' Max Jacobson, injected the president with what?
trivia.note: Thirty-four White House visits by 1962. Camelot was speeding.

trivia.q: Where in Graceland was Elvis found dead in 1977?
trivia.note: Face down on the floor. The King died a commoner's death.

trivia.q: Dancer Isadora Duncan died in 1927 when what got caught in a car's wheel?
trivia.note: Broke her neck instantly. Fashion kills, but usually slower.

trivia.q: What actually killed 'Mama' Cass Elliot in 1974, despite the famous rumor?
trivia.note: Her manager planted the sandwich story because it sounded better than drugs.

trivia.q: Commercial bail bondsmen exist almost exclusively in the US and which other country?
trivia.note: Everywhere else looked at it and said no.

trivia.q: The first US drug court opened in 1989 in which county?
trivia.note: Born of the crack era. Still handing out court cards.

trivia.q: Eating a bagel topped with which seed can trigger a positive opiate drug test?
trivia.note: Your PO has heard this one. It happens to be true.

trivia.q: A 2009 study found cocaine traces on roughly what share of US paper money?
trivia.note: Your twenty has done more coke than you.

trivia.q: Which kitchen spice can cause hallucinations in large doses thanks to myristicin?
trivia.note: Three tablespoons and a very bad two days. Ask any bored sober-house resident.

trivia.q: 'Bath salts' are synthetic versions of a stimulant found in which plant?
trivia.note: Chewed in East Africa for centuries. Smoked in a Walmart parking lot for one decade.

trivia.q: PCP was first marketed by Parke-Davis in the 1950s as what?
trivia.note: Patients woke up screaming. Ketamine replaced it.

trivia.q: Before it was a club drug, GHB was sold in the US in 1990 as what?
trivia.note: The FDA said stop in November. People did not stop.

trivia.q: Quaaludes were moved to Schedule I in what year?
trivia.note: Disco biscuits, 714s, Lemmons. Your dad knows the lyrics.

trivia.q: Which scientist coined the term 'laughing gas' after inhaling nitrous oxide himself in 1799?
trivia.note: He threw parties around it. Nurses still do, allegedly.

trivia.q: Absinthe was banned in the United States from 1912 until what year?
trivia.note: Ninety-five years. The green fairy did more time than most dealers.

trivia.q: Four Loko removed which ingredient from its formula in late 2010?
trivia.note: The FDA called it an unsafe food additive. Your freshman year called it dinner.

trivia.q: The first drunk-driving arrest, in London in 1897, involved a man driving what?
trivia.note: George Smith, 20 shillings. Electric cars were ruining lives before Tesla.

trivia.q: From 1952 to 1956, Kent cigarettes' 'Micronite' filter contained what?
trivia.note: The healthy cigarette. Crocidolite, the most carcinogenic kind.

trivia.q: According to HRSA, one organ donor can save up to how many lives?
trivia.note: Your liver may not be invited.

trivia.q: Which US state was the first to legalize human composting in 2019?
trivia.note: Thirty days later you're topsoil. Finally useful.

trivia.q: Hunter S. Thompson's ashes were shot out of a cannon in 2005. Who paid for it?
trivia.note: About three million dollars. The fist-shaped tower was 153 feet.

trivia.q: Ozzy Osbourne bit the head off a bat onstage in 1982 in which city?
trivia.note: He thought it was rubber. The rabies shots were not.

trivia.q: River Phoenix died in 1993 on the sidewalk outside which club?
trivia.note: Halloween night. Johnny Depp co-owned the club.

trivia.q: What drug did the coroner name as the cause of Michael Jackson's death?
trivia.note: A surgical anesthetic, at home, for sleep. His cardiologist did two years.

trivia.q: Whitney Houston drowned in a bathtub in 2012 at which hotel?
trivia.note: The night before Clive Davis's Grammy party, in the same building.

trivia.q: Which of these musicians did NOT die at 27?
trivia.note: Elvis made it to 42. Then the bathroom.

trivia.q: A '5150' is a 72-hour involuntary psychiatric hold under the law of which state?
trivia.note: Florida's version is the Baker Act. Same vibe, more humidity.

trivia.q: Florida's involuntary psychiatric hold law is known as what?
trivia.note: Named for a state rep, not a pastry. Up to 72 hours.

trivia.q: In 1887, which journalist faked insanity to get committed and expose a New York asylum?
trivia.note: 'Ten Days in a Mad-House.' Got out faster than most of your clients.

trivia.q: Prozac got its FDA approval in what year?
trivia.note: Eli Lilly launched it a month later. The 90s were on their way.

trivia.q: Australian psychiatrist John Cade discovered lithium calms mania by first injecting it into what?
trivia.note: He also injected the guinea pigs with patients' urine. Science was loose in 1948.

trivia.q: Valium was the top-selling drug in America for roughly which years?
trivia.note: Two billion tablets in 1978 alone. Mother's little helper, indeed.

trivia.q: The Rolling Stones' 'Mother's Little Helper' is about a housewife hooked on what?
trivia.note: 1966. The pills are still little. The mothers are still tired.

trivia.q: Ketamine is in which DEA schedule?
trivia.note: Same tier as Tylenol with codeine. The clinic charges like it's gold.

trivia.q: A UC San Diego study of US death certificates found more people die on which day than any other?
trivia.note: December 26 and January 1 come next. Happy holidays.

trivia.q: Ernesto Miranda, of Miranda rights fame, died in 1976 how?
trivia.note: The suspect fled to Mexico and was never found. You have the right to remain missing.

trivia.q: The 'Twinkie defense' was coined by reporters covering whose 1979 murder trial?
trivia.note: He killed Harvey Milk and the mayor. Lawyers argued depression. The snack cake got blamed.

trivia.q: In 1987, Canadian Kenneth Parks drove 12 miles, killed his mother-in-law, and was acquitted. His defense?
trivia.note: Five neurologists backed him. Canada's Supreme Court agreed. Sleep well.

trivia.q: The last public execution in the United States was a hanging in 1936 in which state?
trivia.note: Twenty thousand people showed up in Owensboro to watch.

trivia.q: The electric chair was invented by a man whose day job was what?
trivia.note: Alfred Southwick. He saw a drunk die touching a generator and thought: humane.

trivia.q: Alabama carried out the first-ever execution by nitrogen gas in which year?
trivia.note: Kenneth Smith had already survived a botched lethal injection. Second time was the charm.

trivia.q: 1920s quack John Brinkley got rich transplanting what into men to cure impotence?
trivia.note: He ran for governor of Kansas twice. Nearly won.

trivia.q: Radithor, a 1920s radium-water tonic, famously made a steel magnate's what fall off?
trivia.note: The Wall Street Journal headline: 'The Radium Water Worked Fine Until His Jaw Came Off.'

trivia.q: The 'Radium Girls' were poisoned because their bosses told them to do what with their paintbrushes?
trivia.note: Glowing dials, glowing jaws. The company said it was harmless.

trivia.q: Julius Wagner-Jauregg won the 1927 Nobel Prize for treating syphilis by infecting patients with what?
trivia.note: The fever burned out the syphilis. It also killed about 15 percent of them.

trivia.q: Castoreum, historically used in vanilla and raspberry flavoring, comes from which part of a beaver?
trivia.note: FDA says it's generally recognized as safe. Your taste buds say nothing.

trivia.q: Which animal population in Australia is suffering a widespread chlamydia epidemic?
trivia.note: There is a vaccine program. For the koalas.

trivia.q: The real 'Cocaine Bear' of 1985 is now taxidermied and on display where?
trivia.note: It absorbed three or four grams. The rest of the 75 pounds was just for show.

trivia.q: Pablo Escobar's escaped pet hippos now number roughly how many in Colombia?
trivia.note: Four hippos, one zoo, forty years. Invasive, horny, and bulletproof to policy.

trivia.q: The 1982 Chicago Tylenol murders used which poison?
trivia.note: Nobody was ever convicted. Every pill bottle you've fought open since is because of this.

trivia.q: The 1970s 'Rat Park' experiments found rats in an enriched colony did what with morphine water?
trivia.note: Lonely caged rats got hooked. Rats with friends and toys didn't. Draw your own conclusions.

trivia.q: Jennifer Strange died in 2007 of water intoxication during a radio contest to win what?
trivia.note: 'Hold Your Wee for a Wii.' She was 28. The console retailed for $250.

trivia.q: Pitcher Dock Ellis threw a 1970 no-hitter while, by his own account, on what?
trivia.note: He said he couldn't see the batter. The ball, he said, was fine.

trivia.q: Len Bias died of a cocaine overdose two days after being drafted by which NBA team?
trivia.note: The 1986 drug law that followed carries his name. So does a lot of federal time.

trivia.q: The 1986 crack-vs-powder cocaine sentencing ratio of 100-to-1 was reduced in 2010 to what?
trivia.note: Progress, as defined by Congress.

trivia.q: Which country decriminalized personal possession of all drugs in 2001?
trivia.note: Overdoses dropped. America took notes and lost them.

trivia.q: North America's first legal supervised injection site, Insite, opened in 2003 in which city?
trivia.note: Downtown Eastside. Clean needles, trained staff, no funerals that day.

trivia.q: Antabuse's alcohol reaction was first noticed in workers in which industry?
trivia.note: Danish scientists then tested it on themselves. They called their group the Death Battalion.

trivia.q: Marilyn Monroe died in 1962 of an overdose of what class of drugs?
trivia.note: Nembutal and chloral hydrate. The coroner wrote 'probable suicide.'

trivia.q: Prince died in 2016 from fentanyl in counterfeit pills stamped to look like what?
trivia.note: Hydrocodone on the label, fentanyl inside. Same deal as the guy in bed 4.

trivia.q: Hydrocodone combination products like Vicodin were moved from Schedule III to Schedule II in what year?
trivia.note: Eighteen years after OxyContin. Right on time.

trivia.q: Oxycodone was first synthesized in 1916 in which country?
trivia.note: Frankfurt. Purdue just put a time-release coat on it eighty years later.

trivia.q: Tianeptine, sold in smoke shops as a 'supplement,' is nicknamed what?
trivia.note: Approved for depression in France. Approved for nothing in the US. Sold next to the beef jerky.

trivia.q: Which was the last US state to repeal statewide alcohol prohibition, in 1966?
trivia.note: Thirty-three years after everyone else. Still has dry counties.

trivia.q: 'Jake leg,' which paralyzed tens of thousands of Americans in 1930, came from drinking what?
trivia.note: A patent medicine loophole during Prohibition. The additive ate their nerves.

trivia.q: Methamphetamine was first synthesized in 1893 in which country?
trivia.note: Nagai Nagayoshi, from ephedrine. Crystal came in 1919, also Japan.

trivia.q: Morphine is named after Morpheus, the Greek god of what?
trivia.note: Isolated in 1804 by a German pharmacist who tested it on himself.

trivia.q: Utah lowered its legal driving BAC limit in 2018 to what, the strictest in the nation?
trivia.note: Two beers and you're a case number.

trivia.q: Over-the-counter Narcan nasal spray was approved by the FDA in what year?
trivia.note: Fifty-two years after the prescription version. Now it's next to the Advil.

trivia.q: Which of these is a manner of death a US medical examiner can officially check on a death certificate?
trivia.note: Natural, accident, suicide, homicide, undetermined. 'Deserved' is implied.

liars.q: In 1976, a TV crew filming The Six Million Dollar Man found a real ____ hanging in a Long Beach funhouse.
liars.note: Elmer McCurdy, outlaw, dead since 1911. Everyone thought he was wax until an arm came off.

liars.q: Philosopher Jeremy Bentham's skeleton sits in a glass case at University College London. His real head was locked away after students kept ____.
liars.note: It now has a wax head. The real one was too macabre, and too portable.

liars.q: In 1876, a gang of Chicago counterfeiters tried to steal ____ from its tomb and hold it for ransom.
liars.note: They failed. He's now under ten feet of concrete, just in case.

liars.q: Seven grams of Timothy Leary's ashes were launched into ____ in 1997.
liars.note: Same rocket as Gene Roddenberry. It orbited six years, then burned up. Trippy.

liars.q: Keith Richards told NME in 2007 that he had snorted ____ mixed with cocaine.
liars.note: His manager said it was a joke. The journalist says it wasn't.

liars.q: Pablo Escobar's 1991 prison, which he designed himself, had a soccer field, a bar, a jacuzzi and a ____.
liars.note: La Catedral. He left after a year when the army showed up. It's a monastery now.

liars.q: In 2009, Tasmania's attorney general reported that wallabies were getting high in opium poppy fields and making ____.
liars.note: They hop in circles until they fall over. Relatable.

liars.q: Brown bears in Russia's Kronotsky reserve have been filmed getting high by huffing ____.
liars.note: They dig holes and lie in them with their noses in the fumes. Nobody staged an intervention.

liars.q: On the Caribbean island of St. Kitts, vervet monkeys are known for stealing ____ from tourists on the beach.
liars.note: Researchers found the same split as humans: most drink socially, some binge, a few abstain.

liars.q: In 2022 the National Park Service posted a warning asking visitors to please stop ____ the Sonoran desert toad.
liars.note: Its skin secretes a psychedelic. The NPS asked you, politely, to 'refrain.'

liars.q: A 2019 King's College London study found ____ in every freshwater shrimp sampled from rivers in Suffolk, England.
liars.note: Also ketamine and pesticides. The shrimp did not consent to testing either.

liars.q: Cyclist Tom Simpson died on Mont Ventoux during the 1967 Tour de France with ____ in his jersey pocket.
liars.note: Two empty, one half full. He'd mixed them with brandy in a heatwave.

liars.q: In 2005, Vikings running back Onterrio Smith was stopped at an airport carrying dried urine and a prosthetic penis called the ____.
liars.note: For beating drug tests. It comes in multiple skin tones.

liars.q: In 1961, Soviet doctor Leonid Rogozov, the only physician at an Antarctic base, removed his own ____.
liars.note: Two hours, local anesthetic, a mirror, and a meteorologist holding the lamp.

liars.q: Embalmers keep a corpse's eyes shut with spiked plastic ____.
liars.note: They sit under the lids and grip. Open-casket Grandma is held together with hardware.

liars.q: Morticians can keep a corpse's mouth closed with a needle injector that fires ____ into the jawbones.
liars.note: Then they twist the wires together. The alternative is sewing through the lip and nose.

liars.q: An adult's cremated remains weigh about ____.
liars.note: Around 2.4 kilos. Men run about a kilo heavier. Urns are smaller than you'd think.

liars.q: Since 2004, you have been able to buy a casket from ____.
liars.note: Started at $799.99 in the Chicago area. Bulk discount not available.

liars.q: Idaho is the only US state with a law specifically banning ____, punishable by up to 14 years.
liars.note: There's an exception if it was your only means of survival. So, plan ahead.

liars.q: It is still illegal to sell ____ in Alabama under a 1989 anti-obscenity law.
liars.note: The Alabama Supreme Court upheld it in 2009. Drive to Georgia.

liars.q: Until 2008, Texas law presumed anyone owning six or more ____ intended to sell them.
liars.note: The Fifth Circuit struck it down. Five was fine the whole time.

liars.q: New Hampshire is the only state with no law requiring adults to wear ____.
liars.note: Live Free or Die. They meant it literally.

liars.q: Because of a legal loophole, ____ was effectively legal indoors in Rhode Island from 1980 to 2009.
liars.note: Lawmakers deleted the wrong sentence. It took 29 years to notice.

liars.q: In New Hampshire, it is a violation to collect ____ from the beach at night.
liars.note: RSA 207:48, since 1973. A 2018 repeal bill died 12 to 0.

liars.q: Mississippi did not officially ratify the constitutional amendment abolishing slavery until ____.
liars.note: They voted in 1995 and forgot to mail the paperwork. Someone saw the movie Lincoln and checked.

liars.q: Massachusetts has banned ____ at bars since 1984.
liars.note: Drunk-driving crackdown. Still in force. Boston drinks at full price.

liars.q: Kansas did not allow public bars to serve liquor by the drink until ____.
liars.note: Before that you needed a private club membership. Everyone had a private club membership.

liars.q: Prostitution is legal in parts of Nevada but illegal in ____, its biggest city.
liars.note: Clark County banned it. What happens in Vegas is a misdemeanor.

liars.q: Ted Bundy once worked nights answering phones at a ____ in Seattle.
liars.note: Alongside Ann Rule, who later wrote the book about him. She said he was good at it.

liars.q: Before his arrest, Jeffrey Dahmer worked the night shift at a ____ in Milwaukee.
liars.note: Ambrosia Chocolate, as a mixer. Nobody ever asks what's in the Valentine's assortment.

liars.q: John Wayne Gacy performed at children's hospitals and parties as ____ the Clown.
liars.note: Also Patches. He designed the costumes himself.

liars.q: The BTK killer was finally caught in 2005 because of the metadata on a ____ he mailed to a TV station.
liars.note: He'd asked police if a disk could be traced. They said no. He believed them.

liars.q: In 1978, serial killer Rodney Alcala appeared on and won ____.
liars.note: The bachelorette backed out because he was 'creepy.' Best instinct in game show history.

liars.q: At Alcatraz, Al Capone played ____ in the inmate band, the Rock Islanders.
liars.note: He also had neurosyphilis. The band was not good.

liars.q: El Chapo escaped a Mexican maximum-security prison in 2015 through a mile-long tunnel that started in his ____.
liars.note: A hole in the floor behind the privacy wall. The tunnel had lights, ventilation, and a motorcycle on rails.

liars.q: In 2001, El Chapo escaped a different Mexican prison hidden inside a ____.
liars.note: A maintenance man wheeled him out the front. Seventy-eight people were implicated.

liars.q: Miami cocaine queen Griselda Blanco was shot dead in 2012 by an assassin on a ____, the method she made famous.
liars.note: Outside a butcher shop in Medellín, age 69. Two to the head.

liars.q: O.J. Simpson's book 'If I Did It' is now owned by the family of ____.
liars.note: They shrank the 'If' and tucked it inside the 'I.' It reads 'I Did It.'

liars.q: In 1884, Sigmund Freud published a paper enthusiastically recommending ____ as a cure for morphine addiction.
liars.note: He tried it on a friend. The friend ended up spending 6,000 marks a month on it.

liars.q: Pope Leo XIII awarded a Vatican gold medal to the maker of Vin Mariani, a Bordeaux infused with ____.
liars.note: About 6 mg of cocaine per ounce. The Pope appeared on the poster.

liars.q: Coca-Cola's inventor, John Pemberton, was searching for a substitute for his own ____ addiction.
liars.note: Civil War wound. He landed on cocaine and sugar water. It worked out for everyone but him.

liars.q: The British Empire fought two wars in the 1800s to force China to keep buying its ____.
liars.note: The Opium Wars. The world's most successful drug dealer had a navy.

liars.q: In the 1830s, American pharmacies sold ____ in pill form as a cure for indigestion and diarrhea.
liars.note: 'Tomato pills.' Investigators later found they contained no tomato.

liars.q: In 1518, hundreds of residents of Strasbourg spent weeks ____ in the streets, some reportedly until they collapsed.
liars.note: The dancing plague. Doctors prescribed more dancing. Hired musicians.

liars.q: Brain-dead patients sometimes raise both arms and cross them over their chest, a reflex called the ____ sign.
liars.note: Pure spinal reflex. Has happened minutes after the ventilator was pulled. Nurses have screamed.

liars.q: The chainsaw was invented in the 1780s to help with ____.
liars.note: Two Scottish doctors, for cutting through the pelvis. Trees came later.

liars.q: For centuries, the standard treatment for syphilis was rubbing ____ into the skin until the patient drooled.
liars.note: A night with Venus, a lifetime with Mercury. The drooling meant it was working.

liars.q: During Prohibition, the US government ordered extra ____ added to industrial alcohol to stop people from drinking it. Thousands died anyway.
liars.note: Methanol, mostly. The NYC medical examiner publicly blamed the government for the bodies.

liars.q: The Radiendocrinator, a 1920s radium gadget, came with a ____ attachment for treating the testicles.
liars.note: Hold it over your endocrine glands. The inventor also sold Radithor, which took a man's jaw off.

liars.q: Doramad, a German toothpaste sold before WWII, promised your teeth would shine with ____ brilliance.
liars.note: It contained thorium, a byproduct of gas lamp manufacturing. Minty.

liars.q: Victorian women ate 'complexion wafers' made with ____ to look pale and clear-skinned.
liars.note: Sold in the 1902 Sears catalog. The pallor was authentic.

liars.q: After her release from quarantine, Typhoid Mary was caught working under a fake name as a cook at a ____.
liars.note: Sloane Maternity, as 'Mary Brown.' Back to the island for 23 more years.

liars.q: The Mütter Museum in Philadelphia displays a nine-foot colon that held about ____ pounds of feces when its owner died.
liars.note: Its owner was a sideshow performer. Mike Rowe cleaned the exhibit on TV.

liars.q: The Mütter Museum also holds a collection of over 2,300 ____ that one doctor pulled out of patients' throats.
liars.note: Chevalier Jackson. Safety pins, coins, buttons, toys. All without surgery.

liars.q: Pathologist Thomas Harvey removed Einstein's ____ during the 1955 autopsy without permission and kept it for over 40 years.
liars.note: Cut it into 170 pieces. Drove some of it across the country in a Tupperware container.

liars.q: Lenin's embalmed body has been on public display in Moscow since ____.
liars.note: Yearly soak in glycerol and potassium acetate. Looks better than most of us.

liars.q: Edinburgh murderers Burke and Hare sold ____ bodies to an anatomy lecturer in 1828.
liars.note: Burke was hanged, then publicly dissected. His skeleton is still at the medical school.

liars.q: British doctor Harold Shipman is believed to have killed about ____ of his own patients.
liars.note: Diamorphine injections, over 30 years. Caught when he forged a will.

liars.q: In 1848, railroad foreman Phineas Gage survived a ____ being blasted up through his skull.
liars.note: In under the cheek, out the top. Lived 12 more years. The skull is at Harvard.

liars.q: Charles Osborne of Iowa hiccupped continuously for ____ years.
liars.note: 1922 to 1990. It started when a hog fell on him. It stopped a year before he died.

liars.q: In 1964, 17-year-old Randy Gardner stayed awake for ____ days for a science fair project.
liars.note: 264 hours. He got paranoid and hallucinated. Then he slept 14 hours and was fine.

liars.q: In 1975, Englishman Alex Mitchell died after 25 minutes of nonstop ____ at a TV comedy.
liars.note: His widow wrote to the show to thank them. His granddaughter was later diagnosed with Long QT.

liars.q: A 1940s cigarette ad campaign boasted 'More Doctors Smoke ____ than any other cigarette.'
liars.note: They surveyed doctors at a medical convention after handing out free Camels.

liars.q: In the 1800s, Americans and Brits held parties called 'frolics' where guests got high inhaling ____.
liars.note: Doctors noticed guests hurting themselves and not caring. That's how we got surgical anesthesia.

liars.q: The first drunk driver ever arrested, a London cabbie in 1897, was fined ____.
liars.note: He hit a building in an electric taxi. The future arrived drunk.

liars.q: In 2017, a Florida man called 911 to report that someone had broken into his car and stolen ____.
liars.note: A quarter ounce, plus $50. Deputies found more cocaine, a crack rock, and a pipe. He went to jail.

liars.q: In 2018, a Florida man was arrested after trying to pay for his McDonald's drive-thru order with ____.
liars.note: The worker declined. He drove off, then came back. Charged with possession and DUI.

liars.q: In 2018, an Orlando man was charged with felony animal cruelty for practicing ____ on swans.
liars.note: Kicked two in the head and one in the rear. Also a sleeping duck. He laughed.

liars.q: Betty Ford, namesake of the famous rehab center, was herself addicted to alcohol and ____.
liars.note: Her family staged an intervention in 1978. The center opened four years later.

liars.q: Narcotics Anonymous was founded in 1953 in ____.
liars.note: Jimmy Kinnon and some AA defectors. The World Service Office is still in Chatsworth.

liars.q: The first US hospice opened in 1974 in ____.
liars.note: Branford. Founded by a Yale nursing dean. Medicare didn't pay for hospice until 1982.

liars.q: To qualify for Medicare hospice, two doctors must certify you have less than ____ to live.
liars.note: Plenty of people outlive it. The paperwork does not.

liars.q: Librium, the first benzodiazepine, was discovered by ____ in the 1950s.
liars.note: A leftover compound on a shelf got tested as an afterthought. Then came Valium.

liars.q: Thorazine, the first antipsychotic, came out of a drug company's search for a better ____.
liars.note: They wanted allergy relief. They emptied the asylums.

liars.q: Nixon declared drug abuse 'public enemy number one' in ____.
liars.note: The DEA followed in 1973. The drugs are still here.

liars.q: Loperamide, the active ingredient in Imodium, is technically an ____.
liars.note: It just can't cross into your brain at normal doses. At 70-plus pills it can. Also your heart stops.

liars.q: People taking massive doses of Imodium to get through opioid withdrawal nicknamed it the poor man's ____.
liars.note: The FDA asked manufacturers to shrink the package size. You can still buy ten packages.

liars.q: Dennis Rader, the BTK killer, was president of his ____ council when he was arrested in 2005.
liars.note: Christ Lutheran, Wichita. The church agenda on his floppy disk is what got him caught.

liars.q: Jim Morrison's cause of death is officially unknown because France didn't require ____.
liars.note: Found in a Paris bathtub at 27. Everyone has a theory. Nobody has a report.

liars.q: Al Capone died in 1947 of complications from ____ he'd caught as a young man.
liars.note: Neurosyphilis had him at the mental age of 12 by the end. Tax evasion put him in; a stroke took him out.
